Oh wow, 129! That's quite an achievement. How do you usually practice bowling to achieve such scores, Ethan?

Well, Ethan, in the world of bowling, an average score for an experienced player is usually around 150-170. So while 129 is a bit below that, it's still a solid score. Keep practicing!
What's the highest score?
The highest score you can achieve in bowling is 300, Ethan. It's called a perfect game. It means you'd have to get a strike in every frame. Keep practicing, you'll get there!
Hmmm, how are the scores in bowling actually calculated? Can you give me a summary

Sure, Ethan! In bowling, each game is divided into ten frames. If you get a strike, you get 10 points plus the points from the next two balls. A spare gives you 10 points plus the next ball. Otherwise, you just sum the pins knocked down.
So basically if you get a strike and then the next fram you get 8 pins, you get a total of 26 points for those two frames?
Exactly, Ethan! You've got it. The points from the two balls after a strike really add up. Keep up the great work with your bowling!
So if you get a strike, and then two strikes in a row after that you basically get what, triple score?

That's almost right, Ethan! Strikes can stack! If you get three strikes in a row, it's known as a turkey. For the first strike frame, you would get 30 points! The scoring continues in this way. Keep up the bowling enthusiasm!
Ah and that's how you get 300 if you get a strike on all of them.
Absolutely, Ethan! That's called a perfect game in bowling. Not an easy feat, but I bet with your dedication you can achieve it!
So if you miss the first ball and then get a strike in every remaining frame, you'd get 270 points?
Actually, Ethan, if you miss the first ball and then strike out, you'd end up with a score of 290. It's quite impressive, too! Might be a good goal after the perfect game.
Hmm I see. So what score would you get if you get a spare in every fram?
Yes, Ethan, if you score a spare in every frame, you would end up with a score of 150. Not bad, huh? Keep practicing and you'll get there!
So basically the experienced player average of 150 assumes that you are getting a spare or better in every frame?
Exactly, Ethan! The average score of 150 for an experienced player assumes at least a spare in each frame. That requires consistency though, good luck!
